title: introduce-intake-lineage-resolver-and-compact-release-excerptor
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Adds an intake lineage resolver and compact release excerpt generator: computes model+dataset provenance, hardware affinity, and automated compact changelog snippets that surface performance/cost impact and suggested mitigations. Includes migration/backfill for existing manifests and a CLI hook for one-off annotations.
description:
Summary: Introduce a lightweight intake-lineage resolver and a compact release-excerptor that automatically synthesizes short changelog snippets from model onboarding metadata and performance deltas. The resolver binds model artifacts (tarball IDs), training-run IDs, dataset manifests, container hashes, and hardware affinity fingerprints into a canonical lineage record. The excerptor uses lineage + profile deltas to draft a concise release blurb (1-3 bullets) highlighting: perf changes, latency/cost delta, likely root cause (data, architecture, quantization), and suggested roll-forward/rollback mitigation.

Motivation: Teams repeatedly ask for a quick, reliable explanation of why a model's on-host performance changed across variants. Creating a machine-readable provenance chain plus an automated "release excerpt" reduces manual triage and speeds safe rollouts.

What this PR does (high level):
  - Adds a new module registry/lineage/resolver with an interface to hydrate lineage from intake payloads or from stored training metadata.
  - Adds schema bump v2 for model_manifest to include optional provenance fields (training_run_id, dataset_manifest_ref, container_hash, hardware_fingerprint).
  - Adds migration script migrations/2026_01_backfill_lineage.py to backfill lineage for recent onboardings (with a dry-run flag).
  - Adds a worker web/hooks/release_excerptor.py that subscribes to profile-change events and emits a compact markdown snippet into the release_notes draft stream.
  - Adds CLI integration rmodel lineage annotate and rmodel release draft to preview excerpts locally.
  - Adds unit/integration tests and docs explaining the new fields and operational guidance.

Implementation details:
  - Lineage resolver: conservative merge strategy: prefer explicit fields from onboarding payload; fallback to training run metadata via training-run-api; attach a provenance hash to manifest (sha256 of canonicalized lineage) so downstream systems can quickly diff.
  - Excerptor heuristics: compares baseline and candidate performance profiles (latency p50/p95, token cost per 1k, quality score delta when available). Uses lightweight rule-based scoring (no ML) to construct 2-3 sentence blurb ranked by impact score. Rules are configurable via registry/config/excerptor.yml.
  - Migration/backfill: script runs in batches, emits a reconciliation report (success/failure per manifest) and tags ambiguous cases for human review (created a new curation queue).
  - Rollout: feature gated behind registry.feature_flags.lineage and excerptor.enabled. Default off for older tenants until migrated.

Test plan:
  - Unit tests for resolver (tests/test_lineage_resolver.py) including canonicalization and hash stability.
  - Integration tests for CLI and worker using small synthetic manifests (tests/integration/test_release_excerptor_integration.py).
  - E2E against a staging event stream to validate excerpt generation and release draft insertion.

Checklist:
  - [x] Schema changes (v2) documented and backwards-compatible when fields are absent.
  - [x] Migration script with dry-run validated on staging.
  - [x] CLI docs and examples added.
  - [x] Tests added + CI green.
  - [x] Feature flags and rollout notes included.

Review conversation (high level):
  - Lara Nguyen: "Nice. Two asks: (1) ensure the canonicalization ordering is stable across python versions, and (2) add a short TTL for lineage cache entries so we don't hold stale training run pointers."
  - Asha (author): "Answered — canonicalization uses json.dumps(..., sort_keys=True) + explicit field whitelist. Added cache TTL config (default 24h) and tests for cross-version stability."
  - Tomás Rivera: "Can we make the excerptor fallback to a 'no-change' blurb if the profile delta is below noise thresholds? We had noise-induced chatter in Canary previously."
  - Asha: "Added a configurable noise floor and a 'no significant change' template; excerptor suppresses drafts below a global threshold unless forced."
  - Evelyn Cho: "Migration looks good but please ensure dry-run produces a CSV we can hand to SRE for manual remediation."
  - Asha: "Migration now emits CSV plus a JSON summary blob for the UI import queue."
